title: At least 8 dead after avalanche triggers catastrophic flash floods in Nepal - NBC 7 San Diego
description: At least 8 dead after avalanche triggers catastrophic flash floods in Nepal  NBC 7 San Diego
publisher.title: NBC 7 San Diego
full_article:
Hundreds of people were reported missing after an avalanche of ice and rock triggered massive flash floods that swept through parts of Nepal on Wednesday, killing at least eight people and causing widespread damage to villages and infrastructure.

Officials said 384 tourists, including 291 from countries including India, the United States, the United Kingdom and Malaysia, were reported missing as a result of the flash flood. Three Americans were among those missing, the Nepal Tourist Board said after examining preliminary data.

Stream San Diego News for free, 24/7, wherever you are with NBC 7. WATCH HERE

The Bhotekoshi River flooded around 9 a.m. Wednesday, destroying several villages as well as roads and hydropower projects, officials said. They issued warnings to residents of several of Nepal’s districts and asked them to stay away from the banks of Bhotekoshi, Trishuli and Narayani rivers.

“We have asked both India and China to help us with the rescue efforts,” said Sasmit Pokharel, a spokesperson for the Nepali government.

The worst affected area, Rasuwa district, witnessed similar flash floods to those in August last year, when a glacial lake in neighboring Tibet overflowed as a result of high temperatures in the mountain region. Nine people lost their lives and critical infrastructure including a bridge connecting the two countries were damaged at the time.

Climate experts at the Kathmandu-based International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development say an avalanche from a glacier likely caused Wednesday's flash flood.

The Lhende Khola River, a tributary of the Bhotekoshi River, witnessed maximum flooding Wednesday, they said.

“The Lhende Khola has flooded twice in 14 months, this time triggered by an ice rock avalanche from a glacier on the Nepal side that blocked the river and released a sudden surge downstream,” said Saswata Sanyal, a disaster risk reduction specialist at the climate research group.

“In a warming Himalaya, early warning is the first line of adaptation,” he added.

The Himalayan region, which crosses Nepal and several nearby countries including India, is especially vulnerable to heavy rains, floods and landslides because the area is warming up faster than the rest of the world due to human-caused climate change. Research has shown that extreme weather events including heat waves, heavy rains and melting glaciers have become more frequent in the region.

Researchers at the Kathmandu research group found earlier this year that glaciers across the Hindu Kush Himalaya region are melting at an accelerating rate, with ice loss rates doubling since 2000 primarily due to rising global temperatures and climate change.

title: Huge Flash Flood On Tibet-Nepal Border, Hundreds of Mount Kailash Tourists Missing - Explorersweb »
description: Huge Flash Flood On Tibet-Nepal Border, Hundreds of Mount Kailash Tourists Missing  Explorersweb »
publisher.title: Explorersweb »
full_article:
Hundreds are feared dead after a flash flood from Tibet caused the Bhote Koshi River in Nepal to burst its banks. The flooding has caused massive destruction in the Rasuwa district (Langtang area). The Tibetan side of the border was also badly hit, with buildings completely swept away.

A map shows affected areas. Photo: Google Gemini

The flood hit the Syabrubesi and Timure villages. The swollen river swept away the customs office in Timure. The tsunami-like flash flood continued down the riverbed, hitting populated areas, as seen in videos shot by shocked locals:

https://explorersweb.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/flood-02.mp4

Nepal’s government has deployed army helicopters, but in some areas the water level is still too high for them to land. The flood has covered narrow fluvial gullies with several meters of mud and debris. The government has mobilized the country’s security forces, but ground access is not an option as flooding has cut many roads.





Play



In Tibet, cameras near Gyirong, on the border with Nepal, show the catastrophic scale of destruction:

https://explorersweb.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/flood-01.mp4

Chinese President Xi Jinping has also mobilized extensive search and rescue efforts. “Major losses are feared at Gyirong border port,” Xinhua news reported.

According to The Himalayan Times , authorities are still investigating whether a glacial lake outburst flood caused the surge, or if it was the result of another phenomenon. Though the cause is not yet clear, CNN reports that the draining of a glacial lake led to deadly floods last year.

Nearly 400 travelers missing

Hundreds are missing, and authorities fear many fatalities. Among the missing are many foreigners, including trekkers and pilgrims on their way to Mount Kailash. Nepal’s Tourism Board has released a list of trekking companies whose clients are unaccounted for. The list shows that at least 105 Indian nationals and 37 non-resident Indians (NRIs) are among 384 tourists and travelers missing. Authorities note these are only preliminary numbers.

The number of missing foreigners provided by Nepal trekking companies. Photo: Nepal Tourism Board

The World Health Organization is preparing to send medicine and equipment for around 1,000 people, along with 15 emergency tents. The Ministry of Health has reserved 100 emergency beds at Bir Hospital and the Trauma Centre in Kathmandu, deployed six doctors and two nurses, and is sending an ambulance with medical supplies to affected areas, according to The Himalayan Times .

Hundreds were missing after torrential floods in the Himalayan border areas of Nepal and Tibet destroyed roads, ⁠bridges and power projects on Wednesday.

At least nine people were killed in the flooding, Reuters reported, as authorities braced for more casualties and worse damage.

The Nepal Tourism Board said 384 travellers, including 291 foreign nationals, were missing.

Houses and roads were swept away in Nepal, while officials in China's Tibet said they feared “major casualties” with people missing in Gyirong county after ⁠a mudslide hit a land crossing between the neighbours.

River levels were too high for rescue helicopters to land in Nepal’s affected areas of Syapru Besi and Timure in the mountainous district of Rasuwa, which has a population of about 50,000, officials said.

Television channels broadcast images ​of crumbled homes in the flood waters, floating cars and a metal bridge being washed away, while witnesses told Reuters that entire villages had been engulfed.

“There could be heavy casualties or loss of property,” said district administrator Narendra Pariyar, who urged dwellers on the banks of the Bhote Koshi river to move to higher ground.

“There is devastation everywhere we look,” Tula Bahadur BK, a health worker in Rasuwa, told Reuters. “The settlements next to the river have been completely swept away. Five of my own relatives are missing.”

Nepal's rescue helicopters would be unable to land in the affected areas until the waters recede, army spokesperson Raja Ram Basnet said.

The cause of the flooding was not immediately clear, but a deadly flash flood on the same river last year was eventually traced to the draining of a glacier lake.

China's official Xinhua news agency said the mudslide occurred ​on the Nepali side of the border and hit Gyirong port in Tibet, cutting road, communications and ‌power links in the Shigatse region near the ⁠Chinese border with Nepal.

China's President Xi ​Jinping urged “all-out” search efforts for the missing as well as stronger monitoring and early warning systems to ​prevent secondary disasters.

Nepal's ‌energy ministry said 430MW of electricity supplies were affected, mostly from hydroelectric projects, or more than 12 per cent of the total national ⁠hydropower capacity of 3.2GW, according to a Reuters calculation.

Police and military personnel were joining in the rescue effort, ⁠said Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah.

“Instructions have been given … to move the people living in the lower areas to safer places,” he said. “People along the river are advised to exercise extra caution and remain alert.”

From its origins in Tibet, the Bhote Koshi river empties into Nepal's Trishuli river that eventually flows into India as the Gandak river.

The mudslide is believed to have been caused by a wall of mud and rock that collapsed into a river on the Himalayan border between Nepal and China-controlled Tibet, resulting in catastrophic flooding on the Nepali side that has left at least 17 people dead and over 300 tourists missing.

Though the horrifying disaster is still unfolding, initial reports suggest the floods could be the result of an avalanche triggered by an earthquake, Nepal’s foreign minister Shisir Khanal told the country’s parliament Wednesday.

full_article:
US Geological Survey recorded a magnitude 4.4 earthquake in Tibetan territory at 8.37am



Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.



Floods battered Nepal on Wednesday after a sudden surge in the Bhote Koshi River swept through the Rasuwa district near the China border, killing over 30 people and leaving hundreds of people, including foreign nationals, reported missing.The cause of the devastating flash flood is now being investigated, with an initial assessment suggesting that an ice avalanche may have blocked the Lhende River, causing water to build up before suddenly bursting downstream.According to The Kathmandu Post, Rijan Bhakta Kayastha, a professor at Kathmandu University and climate researcher, said the preliminary assessment was based on discussions with scientists in Nepal and China. He said an ice avalanche from the Nepal side appeared to have fallen into the Lhende River and blocked its flow.“There is information that an ice avalanche from the Nepal side blocked the Lhende river,” Kayastha said, according to The Kathmandu Post. “An earthquake also occurred on the Tibetan side around the same time.”The US Geological Survey recorded a magnitude 4.4 earthquake in Tibetan territory at 8:37am, around 47 kilometres north of Gosainkunda.However, it remains unclear whether the earthquake played any role in triggering the flood.Scientists are also investigating whether a glacial lake outburst contributed to the disaster. Kayastha said it could take several days to establish whether a glacial lake had burst, noting that the region contains several large glacial lakes.A similar disaster struck the area on July 8, 2025, when a sudden flood in the Lhende River was attributed to a glacial lake outburst. Satellite imagery at the time indicated that a glacial lake had burst near the Nepal-China border.The latest flooding struck the Bhote Koshi River at around 8:30am, damaging settlements and infrastructure and sweeping away people and vehicles.Nepal Tourism Board said 384 travellers, including 291 foreign nationals and 93 Nepali nationals, had been reported missing based on preliminary information. Around 105 Indians were among those reported missing, while 37 non-resident Indians were reported missing from the Himalayan Glacier area.Rescue operations continued through Wednesday, with authorities urging residents along the Trishuli River to move to safer areas as floodwaters moved downstream.India has also offered assistance. Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke to Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah and said India was ready to provide “all possible humanitarian assistance”, adding that teams from both countries were coordinating rescue and relief efforts.

UDIN DHUNGA, Nepal — An avalanche of ice and rock triggered massive flash floods in Nepal on Wednesday, August 26, killing at least eight people and leaving hundreds missing. These also caused widespread damage to villages and infrastructure.

Officials said that 384 tourists were reported missing. They included 291 people from countries such as India, the United States, the United Kingdom and Malaysia.

The Bhotekoshi River flooded around 9 a.m. local time Wednesday, destroying several villages, roads and hydropower projects, officials said.

China, India’s help sought in rescue

“We have asked both India and China to help us with the rescue efforts,” said Sasmit Pokharel, a spokesperson for the Nepali government.

Dozens of multi-storied buildings, trucks, and vans were buried under vast quantities of mud in the district of Nuwakot. Officials warned residents in several of Nepal’s districts and asked them to stay away from the banks of the Bhotekoshi, Trishuli, and Narayani rivers.

The Himalayan region, which spans Nepal and nearby countries, including India, is especially vulnerable to heavy rains, floods and landslides. Nepal: A sudden flood in the Bhotekoshi River battered Nepal’s Rasuwa district on Wednesday morning, sweeping through settlements and causing widespread destruction. Houses, bridges and other structures were damaged as muddy floodwaters surged through the area, with several people reported missing.Dramatic visuals circulating on social media show the scale of the flooding, with torrents of brown water rushing through communities and engulfing buildings and bridges. People in areas including Nuwakot, Dhading, Chitwan and Gorkha, particularly those living close to riverbanks, have been advised to evacuate as water levels in the Bhotekoshi River rise.According to a list provided by Nepal’s National Tourism Board, more than 100 Indians and 37 non-resident Indians (NRIs) are reported missing following the disaster.

title: Nepal’s deadliest disasters: From earthquakes to flash floods and avalanches - The Federal
description: Nepal’s deadliest disasters: From earthquakes to flash floods and avalanches  The Federal
publisher.title: The Federal
full_article:
Nepal has suffered repeated earthquakes, avalanches, floods and landslides. Some disasters have killed thousands, while others have devastated remote communities and disrupted access to essential services, with the latest being a deadly flash flood caused by a surge in the Bhote Koshi River that ripped through northern Nepal on Wednesday (August 26) morning, resulting in at least 19 deaths and 105 Indians going missing.

1934 earthquake devastated Nepal

An earthquake of magnitude estimated to be between 7.6 and 8.3 struck near Okhaldhunga on January 15, 1934, resulting in widespread destruction in Kathmandu and eastern Nepal. Mud-brick homes collapsed, while temples and other buildings were severely damaged.

Also Read: 8 dead, 100 Indians missing as flash flood sweeps through Nepal’s Rasuwa district

At least 8,519 people died in Nepal, with thousands more killed in India. According to reports in Reuters and Nepali Times, the Nepali government created a relief office to manage reconstruction in Kathmandu. Aid also came from India, Britain and Japan.

1988 earthquake

A magnitude 6.9 earthquake struck near the Nepal–India border in Udayapur District on August 21 1988, killing about 1,003 people while thousands were injured.

Also Read: What is GLOF, the phenomenon that triggered Sikkim flash floods?

Landslides and floods added to the destruction. Villages across southeastern Nepal were damaged, while an estimated 500,000 people lost their homes. Monsoon rain and poor infrastructure reportedly made relief operations harder for the Nepali Army and international agencies.

2014 Everest avalanche

A huge section of the Khumbu Icefall collapsed on April 18, 2014, triggering an avalanche that swept through camps below Mount Everest.

Thirteen Sherpa guides were killed, while at least three others were missing or presumed buried. Many more were injured. Rescue teams, including Nepalese army helicopters, recovered victims. The disaster halted Everest expeditions for weeks and led Sherpas to demand stronger safety measures and compensation.

2015 earthquake and Everest disaster

A magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck central Nepal near Gorkha district on April 25, 2015, followed by a magnitude 7.3 aftershock on May 12. According to a Reuters report, the combined toll reached about 9,000, making the disaster Nepal’s worst modern catastrophe.

Also Read: What Indian mountaineers feel about Nepal’s likely move to make permission for Everest climb tougher

The April earthquake triggered an avalanche from Pumori that swept into Everest’s South Base Camp. At least 17 people died, and 61 were injured, including climbers and Sherpa guides.

The injured were evacuated through helicopters, reported The Guardian.

May 2015 aftershock

The May 12, 2015 magnitude 7.3 aftershock caused fresh damage in eastern Nepal. Official figures recorded 218 deaths and more than 3,500 injuries, with major losses in Dolakha, Ramechhap and Sindhupalchowk.

Landslides and building collapses blocked routes into remote districts. Helicopters carried relief supplies while road crews worked to reopen access, reported Reuters.

2019 and 2020 monsoon disasters

Heavy monsoon rain caused floods and landslides across central and eastern Nepal in July 2019. Authorities reported 78 deaths, 40 injuries and 32 missing people. More than 17,500 people were displaced, reported the Indian Express.

Also Read: Nepal reels from climate extremes as droughts and floods wreak havoc

The 2020 monsoon brought further destruction. By mid-year, at least 196 people had died, and 188 were injured. Flash floods swept away homes and bridges, while river banks collapsed in the Terai.

2025 floods and avalanche

Heavy rainfall in early October 2025 triggered floods and landslides in eastern Nepal. By October 5, authorities reported 44 deaths and five missing people. Ilam recorded 37 landslide deaths. The Nepali Army used helicopters during rescue operations.

On 4 November, an avalanche struck a base camp on Mount Yalung Ri in Dolakha. Seven people died, including five foreign climbers and two Nepali guides. Poor weather delayed rescue teams, who later recovered the bodies, reported Al Jazeera.

CCTV footage shows people fleeing seconds before a massive mudslide engulfs a crossing on the Nepal-China border, sweeping through roads, buildings and vehicles. At least nine people have been killed and hundreds of people were reported missing after torrential floods.

title: Nepal flash flood from Tibet leaves 17 dead, 105 Indians missing - India Today
description: Nepal flash flood from Tibet leaves 17 dead, 105 Indians missing  India Today
publisher.title: India Today
full_article:
A massive flash flood originating in Tibet swept through central Nepal on Wednesday, killing at least 17 people and leaving hundreds missing, including 105 Indians, as it tore through towns and villages, washed away bridges and damaged hydropower projects. Officials said the flood caused widespread devastation across Rasuwa, Dhading, Nuwakot and Chitwan districts.

Preliminary satellite analysis showed the flood was triggered by a rockslide from an unstable mountain rock mass near the Nepal-Tibet border, around 20 km northeast of the Tibet-Rasuwagadhi border area. Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said the flood entered the Trishuli river through the Bhote Koshi at Timure due to the rockslide and the swelling of the Lhende river on the Nepal-Tibet border. The Department of Hydrology and Meteorology said the flooding was not caused by rainfall in Rasuwa.

Officials said the flood surged through the Bhote Koshi river at around 9 am local time, first affecting Rasuwa and Dhading, before spreading further and damaging at least four permanent bridges and some temporary ones. Rasuwa, near the Tibet border, was the worst-hit area. Videos circulating on social media showed a wall of water at Rasuwagadhi overriding a two-storey building and sweeping away everything in its path. Some footage also showed people running at the sound of the approaching water before the area was engulfed in mud and debris.

The Nepal Home Ministry said the death toll included six people in Dhading, three in Nuwakot and one in Rasuwa. Officials said nearly 500 people were missing. Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal told the House of Representatives that more than 80 security personnel, including 44 Nepal Army personnel, were among those missing. The Nepal Tourism Board said 384 travellers — 291 foreigners and 93 Nepali nationals — had gone missing in the Rasuwa floods. It said 105 Indians and 37 NRIs were among the missing, along with tourists from the US, Malaysia, the UK, South Africa, Australia and the Netherlands. Most of the Indians were headed for the Kailash Manasarovar Yatra in Tibet, and Samrat Tours and Travel said at least 59 of them were pilgrims.

The Indian Embassy in Kathmandu issued emergency numbers for help and information related to affected Indian nationals, asking people to contact +977 985 131 6807 or +977 970 910 7500. In a post on X, it said, "The Embassy of India has remained engaged with the relevant authorities of Government of Nepal for early rescue and relief for Indian nationals affected by the flash floods that took place in Nepal." It added, "Rescue and relief efforts continue to be strengthened in coordination with the Government of Nepal." The Nepal Tourism Board also issued helpline numbers, including toll-free emergency number 1234, hotline 1144 and tourist police number 9851289445.

Warnings remained in place through the day. Nepal’s Flood Forecasting Division said on X: "According to information received from the Chinese side, since the lake at the river blockage site has not yet been fully drained, the risk remains in the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli areas" and asked people to stay away from the rivers and remain in safe places. Later, the NDRRMA said: "Even though the lake has not been fully drained at the site where the river is blocked, the risk persists in the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli areas, and people are urged to stay away from the river and remain in safe locations until the next update is issued." The authority also asked people living near riverbanks in Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Chitwan and Gorkha to stay on high alert and take safety measures until further notice.

The flood badly hit roads, trade infrastructure and power projects. The Kathmandu Post reported that the 42-km road linking Betrawati in Nuwakot with the Rasuwagadhi border crossing in Rasuwa had been washed away. Quoting Department of Roads spokesperson Shubharaj Neupane, it said the floodwaters destroyed the road at multiple points and swept away several concrete bridges. Rasuwa Chief Customs Officer Rajendra Dhungana said numerous vehicles and goods kept at the customs premises were washed away and a recently constructed bridge was destroyed at the key Nepal-Tibet trade point. The Independent Power Producers’ Association Nepal said eight operational hydropower projects with a combined capacity of 354 MW and five projects under construction in Nuwakot and Rasuwa were damaged. Among the major operational projects affected were the 111 MW Rasuwagadhi Hydropower Project, the 78 MW Sanjen Khola Hydropower Project and the 60 MW Upper Trishuli 3A project.

Local officials said the scale of the flooding was unusually large. The Kathmandu Post quoted Uttargaya Rural Municipality deputy chair Chameli Gurung as saying that around a dozen settlements, including Syaphrubesi, Betrawati, Mailung, Salletar, Shantibazar, Pairebesi, Khalti Basti, Sole, Trishuli and Battar, had been affected. Rasuwa Assistant Chief District Officer Dhruva Prasad Adhikari said two settlements had suffered significant damage. A local media report, quoting Nepal Police spokesperson Abi Narayan Kafle, said the Area Police Office in Timure, the police post in Syaphrubesi and the police post at Rasuwagadhi were also damaged. Armed Police Force spokesperson Netra Bahadur Karki said four force personnel had gone missing in Rasuwa.

The Nepal Army, Armed Police Force and Nepal Police were deployed for rescue and relief after an emergency meeting chaired by the Prime Minister to review the situation. The army said it had mobilised 12 helicopters for search and rescue, and rescued six people from Syaphrubesi, two from Mailung and four from Dhunche, all in Rasuwa district. It also set up a treatment centre at Military Training Centre No 1 in Trishuli, where medical personnel were providing emergency treatment, and sent an MI17 helicopter with an Emergency Medical Rescue Team to the district hospital in Trishuli. Security personnel rescued more than 80 stranded people. Five drones and three sniffer dogs were also deployed to support rescue and relief work.

President Ramchandra Paudel expressed sorrow over the loss of life and property in Rasuwa and Nuwakot. The disaster has left large parts of central Nepal badly damaged, with lives lost, hundreds still untraced and major transport, trade and power links hit. Last year too, two catastrophic floods hit the Bhote Koshi in Rasuwa and killed at least 10 people.
